# Turn Your Messy Class Notes into Study Flashcards with Cohere

> **In short:** Cohere's chat can turn a pasted block of lecture notes into a Q&A flashcard set in under a minute. You'll need a free Cohere account, your notes in plain text, and a few minutes to copy and study.

Lecture notes are useful, but they don't test you. Flashcards do — they make you recall the answer before you see it. The painful part is making them. This guide walks you through using Cohere's free chat to skip the typing and get straight to quizzing yourself, so an evening of studying actually sticks.

## Before you start
- A free Cohere account (sign up with an email at cohere.com — no credit card needed)
- Your notes in plain text — copy them from your laptop, Google Doc, or note app
- About 10 minutes total; the actual chat takes under a minute
- A notes app, document, or flashcard tool to paste the finished cards into

## Step 1 — Create a free Cohere account and open the chat
Go to **cohere.com** in your browser and click the **Sign up** or **Get started** button (look for it near the top-right of the page). Enter your email, set a password, and confirm the verification email. After you confirm, you land inside the Cohere dashboard. Look for a chat box or a labeled chat/playground area — it's usually front and center. If you see a row of model options above the chat, leave the default one selected; any of them can turn notes into Q&A pairs.
💬 Example: a one-line email like "yourname@example.com" works fine to create the account.
You'll know it worked when you see a chat box with a text field at the bottom and a blinking cursor ready for your message.

## Step 2 — Open your notes and copy a small section
Open your class notes in a separate window or tab — Google Docs, Word, Notion, or a plain text file all work. Find one topic or sub-section, such as "The Three Branches of the US Government" or "Mitosis — phases and outcome." Highlight just that section and copy it (Ctrl+C on Windows, Cmd+C on Mac). Use a chunk of about 200–500 words at a time; longer chunks mean the AI may skip details or summarize too loosely.
💬 Example: copy only the bullet points about "phases of mitosis," not the whole biology chapter.
You'll know it worked when the notes are in your clipboard and you can paste them anywhere with Ctrl+V or Cmd+V.

## Step 3 — Paste your notes into the chat and ask for flashcards
Click inside the Cohere chat box and paste your notes (Ctrl+V or Cmd+V). On the next line, add a short instruction telling the AI what you want. A simple, clear instruction works best — say how many cards you want, the format, and whether you want answers hidden on the back. Hit **Enter** or click the **Send** button (it usually looks like a paper airplane or arrow).
💬 Example: "Turn these notes into 10 study flashcards. Format each one as: Q: [question] / A: [answer]. Cover the main definitions, dates, and examples."
You'll know it worked when the chat starts typing a response and a numbered or bulleted list of Q&A pairs appears on screen.

## Step 4 — Check the cards and ask for fixes if needed
Give the response a quick read. Each flashcard should have one clear question, one short answer, and no facts that weren't in your notes. If cards are too long, too vague, or skip details, ask for a redo. Be specific about what to change. Cohere doesn't browse the web in chat, so it should only use what you pasted — but always double-check before you trust a card.
💬 Example: "The answer to card 3 is too long. Make every answer under 15 words, and remove any dates I didn't include in the notes."
You'll know it worked when every card has a clean question, a short answer you can verify in your notes, and nothing has been added from outside.

## Step 5 — Copy the flashcards into your study app or a document
Highlight the entire flashcard block in Cohere's reply (click at the start, then Shift+click at the end, or press Ctrl+A / Cmd+A inside the chat panel if the chat allows it). Copy it, then paste it into a doc, a notes app, or a flashcard tool like Anki or Quizlet. Keep the Q: / A: format so each card is easy to import. If you want a printable set, paste into Google Docs and use a table.
💬 Example: paste into a new Google Doc titled "Bio 101 — Mitosis flashcards" so you can find it again later.
You'll know it worked when the cards are saved in a place you can open on your phone or laptop, and the question and answer for each card are clearly separated.

## Step 6 — Study the cards the same day
Open your saved flashcards and quiz yourself: read the question, say the answer out loud or in your head, then flip to check. Sort cards into "got it" and "missed it" piles. Re-quiz the missed ones tomorrow. Flashcards only work if you come back to them — making them with AI saves time, but the learning still happens when you test yourself.
💬 Example: spend 5 minutes quizzing tonight, then 5 more tomorrow morning on the cards you missed.
You'll know it worked when you can answer at least 8 out of 10 cards from memory without looking.

## Common mistakes
- **Pasting a whole textbook chapter at once.** The AI will skip details or lose focus. **Fix:** paste one sub-topic at a time, around 200–500 words per request.
- **Skipping the fact-check step.** Cohere can rephrase or summarize your notes, but it won't catch every typo in your source — and the AI is summarizing, not generating from scratch, so any ambiguity in your notes can show up in the cards. **Fix:** spend a minute comparing each card to your original notes before you save.
- **Saving the cards in the chat only.** If you close the chat or the window, the cards can be hard to find again. **Fix:** copy the finished block into a doc, notes app, or flashcard tool right away.

## What this means for you
- **In everyday life:** if you're studying for a test, a work certification, or even a new language, the same trick works — paste text, ask for Q&A cards, save them, quiz yourself.
- **For your business or work:** if you're onboarding to a new tool or learning a new process, you can paste documentation into Cohere and get self-quiz cards to learn it faster.
- **If you're just getting started:** the easiest first move is to take one page of notes you already have and try this on a single topic tonight.

## Try it now
Open your most recent class notes, copy one sub-topic about 200 words long, paste it into Cohere's chat, and ask for "10 flashcards in Q: / A: format." In two minutes you'll have a small set of cards ready to study — and a system you can reuse for every subject from now on.
